trinity_porter.text: Morning. This is the Wren Library, designed by Sir Christopher Wren and finished in 1695. Mind the floor, it's older than your great-great-grandmother's great-grandmother.
Out in Great Court, students try to run round the whole court while the clock strikes twelve. Twice, as it does. About forty-three seconds. They made a film about it. Not here, as it happens.
Trinity was founded by Henry VIII in 1546. He's above the Great Gate holding a chair leg instead of a sceptre. Some student swapped it years ago and nobody ever swapped it back.

then.text: Go on, find that student. And keep your sticky apple off the Principia.
An apple from the tree! How lovely. Keep it well away from the books, please.
Newton came to Trinity in 1661 as a poor student who waited on richer ones. By 1669 he was a professor. In 1687 he published the Principia, the book that explained gravity and how the planets move.

We keep his own copy here, full of his corrections in the margins. As for the apple: in 1726, an old man now, he told his friend William Stukeley that he'd seen one fall in the garden, and it set him thinking. He never said it hit him.

else.text: The Wren Library. Shhh. The books are sleeping. Some of them have been sleeping since 1695.
